newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian police arrest 56 in riots in capital.
newsitem.headline: Zambian police arrest 56 in riots in capital.

text.p: Zambian police arrested 56 suspects on Wednesday after scores of market traders rioted in the capital for the second time this week.

Police fired teargas and beat rioters when angry youths vandalised property in the central business district after a mysterious fire gutted their sprawling market near the city centre on Tuesday night.
By mid-morning the area was deserted as apprehensive traders closed shops and residents abandoned the city centre. Armed police patrolled the empty streets, ordering people to leave or face arrest.
Police said several people, including four police officers, were injured in skirmishes.
On Monday youths looted shops and besieged the presidential palace after police burnt their wooden vending stalls in an effort by local authorities to clean up the city.
President Frederick Chiluba subsequently assured the vendors they had his support to rebuild their stalls.
But police fighting the rioters on Wednesday destroyed more stalls, sparking outrage from the vendors.
Local authorities have stepped up a campaign against illegal vending following the opening of a new market in the city on Saturday.
The market, built with Israeli government help, has room for only 3,000 of the more than 10,000 vendors in the city.
The government has denied responsibility for the burning of the stalls and has blamed the opposition.
"Government investigations have revealed that (former president) Kenneth Kaunda is behind the burnings," presidential spokesman Richard Sakala told reporters.
By midday calm had returned to the city, but the business district was deserted.
"The situation is under control," a police spokesman said.

Tuesday night's fire is the second to have destroyed public property this week, following a blaze which damaged the first floor of a government building housing vice president Godfrey Miyanda's office.
